Patch 0.41.0.35 (the grave learns the weight of steel)

  • The first bones remain the measure: level 1–10 Skeleton health, damage, and swing timing are unchanged and now anchor the complete enemy progression curve.
  • Higher realms answer post-squish heroes: every Imp, Demon Orc, Construct, Inferno Titan, Moonfrost creature, Cinder Wastes foe, and Stormcrown enemy now grows from one level-based health and damage budget instead of disconnected pre-squish stat blocks.
  • Gear quality changes the shape of a fight: same-level mixed uncommon/rare equipment lands in a steady middle encounter band, low or missing gear creates meaningful pressure, and full legendary, upgraded, potency-enhanced equipment makes ordinary same-level enemies decisively easy.
  • Creature identity survives the squish: glass cannons, bruisers, tanks, and swift attackers retain bounded family-specific health, damage, and movement differences without breaking the shared progression curve.
  • Dungeons no longer demand obsolete numbers: normal packs, elite rooms, sequential bosses, run levels, and Normal/Heroic/Mythic difficulty now compose from the same post-squish foundation; the old million-Vitality and accidental extra ×10 boss assumptions are gone.
  • Elite danger and elite rewards agree: Fire, Air, Verdant, and Abyssal elite-room spawns now carry explicit elite identity alongside their intended combat multiplier, allowing the existing elite loot path to recognize all of them.
  • Slows cannot heal the enemy: applying or expiring temporary movement effects no longer adds player-only level health, replaces authored hostile speed, or enables enemy regeneration during combat.
  • The curve is guarded end to end: server regression coverage checks every overworld family against low, medium, and optimized gear envelopes, preserves the exact Skeleton anchor, and verifies elite, dungeon, boss, run-level, difficulty, and debuff transitions.
  • Clients receive the new balance ledger: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-35.

Patch 0.41.0.34 (two heroines step from the veil)

  • The shadeblade shows her face: the Rogue is now an adult female hero with a sharper faceted face, paired emerald eyes, brows, lips, swept dark hair, a side braid, deeper hood framing, and a more agile shoulder–waist–hip silhouette.
  • The last sun crowns a priestess: the Cleric is now an adult female hero with warm facial features, paired holy eyes, a braided crown and side plaits, a rear coif, and a strong feminine silhouette beneath practical reliquary armor.
  • Armor still fits the bearer: all 18 attachment regions and every equipment family retain exact local and remote placement; default hair and ornaments hide beneath equipped headgear while faces and paired eyes remain readable.
  • Beauty does not change battle: hitboxes, authoritative movement, abilities, animation timing, equipment replication, class balance, and saved characters are unchanged. Dedicated High and Low hardware renders validate both redesigned heroes in every animation state.
  • Clients receive the new silhouettes: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-34.

Patch 0.41.0.33 (the last lantern knows every road)

  • The codeborn redesign is whole: Eidolon's production presentation now follows one generated dark-fantasy language across characters, equipment, enemies, NPCs, summons, loot, realms, Lanternhold, dungeons, abilities, hazards, combat reactions, icons, and interface atmosphere.
  • All four heroes carry their own silhouette: Fighter, Rogue, Wizard, and Cleric use class-shaped procedural rigs with complete locomotion, attack, cast, death, local, remote, equipment-swap, and state-restoration coverage.
  • Every relic keeps its identity: all 36 equippable families render across 14 positions and 18 attachment regions; every current item has a generated menu sigil and all 80 equipment, soulstone, Heart, and Shard identities have an intentional world-drop form.
  • No foe wears a borrowed mask: all 47 current player, service, summon, overworld-enemy, and dungeon-boss archetypes resolve through named rigs; an unknown actor or malformed construction now fails closed instead of becoming a generic hidden fallback.
  • Nine domains remember their names: Gloamwood, Lanternhold, Moonfrost, the Cinder Wastes, Stormcrown, Thorncrypt, the Furnace Below, the Shattered Aerie, and the Drowned Sanctum each retain distinct terrain, architecture, atmosphere, foliage, hazard, encounter, and faction language.
  • Every rite tells the gameplay truth: all 52 selectable abilities, 60 rune variants, projectiles, traps, persistent fields, auras, conditions, boss telegraphs, impacts, and combat reactions use their server-owned shape, timing, direction, and radius—including Spirit Guardians and other boosted or expanded effects.
  • The black pilgrimage is now a production gate: the disposable and live character route visibly enters one canonical sandstorm, lightning zone, lava pool, and wind gust, confirms each exact and unique interest-managed client footprint, receives real authoritative damage, then proves Lanternhold safety; server and gallery gates continue to audit the complete 65-field atlas.
  • Thresholds remain synchronized: full and delta snapshots, local and remote actors, equipment replication, movement smoothing, reconnect, late join, death/respawn, realm and dungeon transitions, scene cleanup, and restored persistent effects retain one authoritative identity.
  • No old painted world waits underneath: production code, manifests, preload lists, service-worker caches, asset packs, and deploy output contain no authored model or raster dependency; the three tiny plant compatibility sentinels contain no geometry and are never referenced by the production runtime.
  • High and Low are both intentional: hardware-browser galleries cover the complete actor, equipment, ability, status, projectile, impact, loot, terrain, architecture, dungeon, and 65-hazard ledgers; Low removes optional ornament without shrinking combat truth or losing identity.
  • The living game remains intact: quests and level-one dailies, combat, item stats and the 25× stat squish, inventory/equipment coexistence, complete vendor sell-all slots, chat tabs/resizing, dynamic windows, economy, progression, and existing saves keep their established behavior.
  • Clients carry the final seal: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-33.

Patch 0.41.0.32 (no wound crosses a forgotten threshold)

  • Hazards no longer multiply behind the veil: repeated full-state and delta snapshots now reconcile the dedicated hazard ledger instead of recreating animated meshes outside the normal entity map; changed footprints replace cleanly, removed or pending hazards cannot reappear, and old geometry is disposed.
  • Scene thresholds close behind you: throttled entity creations are canceled when their authoritative full state removes them and the entire old queue is cleared on realm or dungeon transitions, preventing stale enemies, loot, or effects from materializing in the next scene.
  • Exposure always starts honestly: partial environmental-damage time is cleared on death, respawn, recall, town safety, dungeon entry, world transfer, disconnect, reconnect, explicit removal, and QA teleport; a later return must spend one complete tick inside the danger field.
  • Lanternhold's whole fence line is safe: the server now uses the same inclusive x -100..100 and z 100..300 boundary as the client and world art, while a step beyond it immediately returns to normal overworld rules.
  • Every realm hazard passed inspection: automated server coverage verifies all 65 authoritative anchors—12 Gloamwood sandstorms, 15 Moonfrost lightning zones, 19 Cinder lava pools, and 19 Stormcrown wind gusts—plus their broadcast identity, radii, cadence, and damage configuration.
  • Exact danger survives Low quality: lower settings reduce optional particles and segments across all four active hazard families while preserving the identical server-owned radius, fixed boundary, theme, and warning language.
  • The full blighted atlas is visible: hardware Chrome renders all 65 production footprints together at High and Low, confirms every mesh is attached exactly once, rebuilds the complete gallery without leaks, and checks every transform and radius.
  • Live release retries report recovery correctly: a successful same-route document retry now reconciles an earlier edge-level navigation failure, while an unrecovered failure remains a hard QA error.
  • Combat balance remains untouched: hazard damage percentages, tick intervals, anchor positions, gameplay radii, character stats, quests, progression, saves, and economy values are unchanged.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-32.

Patch 0.41.0.31 (the five realms remember their skin)

  • Every overworld realm now has its own codeborn ground: Gloamwood bears grave-loam, moss veins, cairn chips, and root scars; Lanternhold keeps offset vigil cobbles and amber oath marks; Moonfrost fractures into rimeglass; the Cinder Wastes burn through blackglass faults; and Stormcrown carries conductor-cut storm slate.
  • The world beyond the fences joins the same style: Eidolic blackwater and the restrained star-lit night vault are generated at runtime instead of loading painted image files.
  • Terrain follows the real world geometry: all four realm plates preserve their exact 2,000-by-1,600 gameplay regions, while Lanternhold receives a precisely inset town surface without changing fences, collision, navigation, portals, hazards, spawns, or combat.
  • High and Low remain intentional: deterministic 256- and 128-pixel surface sources retain the same motifs and boundaries, with cached textures and idempotent environment startup preventing duplicate particle systems or repeated network work.
  • Dungeons no longer carry a hidden texture escape hatch: legacy fallback floors and walls now use the generated Gloamwood and Lanternhold materials, and town startup no longer waits on textures it never consumes.
  • The last painted asset vault is gone: nine old terrain/menu images and the bitmap favicon—about 23 MB—have left the production tree and remain recoverable through Git history; automated guards require authored raster count to stay exactly zero.
  • Even the shell is codeborn: login/menu atmosphere uses layered CSS light and haze, while the browser tab carries an inline dark-fantasy SVG sigil with no image request.
  • Device storage now tells the truth: realm terrain is marked built in with no download, all production asset packs are payload-free, and only stale release caches remain clearable.
  • Every surface is inspectable: unit coverage verifies unique deterministic signatures, exact materials and realm footprints, loader-free startup, and idempotency; hardware Chrome captures all six ground families at High and Low while asserting zero authored raster requests.
  • Gameplay and player data are untouched: this is a visual and loading cutover only; stats, movement, quests, item values, abilities, damage volumes, progression, saves, and networking remain authoritative and unchanged.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-31.

Patch 0.41.0.30 (the fallen armory keeps its shape)

  • Loot is no longer a field of anonymous colored orbs: every dropped weapon, offhand, armor piece, accessory, gem, Heart, and Shard now appears as an intentional code-generated dark-fantasy object.
  • What falls is what you can wear: all 36 equippable bases reuse the exact silhouette builder used on local and remote characters, including rarity glow, tier, potency, sockets, socketed gems, set runes, and unique-effect marks.
  • Every soulstone can be read before pickup: all seven gem types preserve their own palette and all six qualities gain progressively richer facet crowns; Low quality removes only optional ornaments, never identity.
  • Rare materials have become relics: Eidolon Hearts float inside an iron soul cage, while Eidolon Shards appear as broken blue purpose-prisms with orbiting fragments.
  • Ground drops share a coherent reliquary: rarity-lit octagonal plinths anchor each item, selection and pickup-range rings remain clear against terrain, and item labels stay upright while the object turns.
  • Pickup feedback can no longer leak between drops: selection uses per-drop visibility and transforms instead of mutating cached shared material opacity, so targeting one item cannot brighten or fade another.
  • Clicking stays stable while art moves: the plinth, upright label, and generous pickup hitbox remain anchored while only the item form bobs and turns; selection scale cannot move the clickable volume or alter the authoritative pickup flow.
  • Long loot sessions no longer invalidate live labels: the text-texture cache is now reference-counted and evicts only idle least-recently-used entries; a texture still displayed in the world is never disposed under cache pressure.
  • The entire dropped-item catalog is gated: unit coverage constructs all 80 exact identities, audits finite bounds and cache lifecycle, and hardware Chrome captures every form at High and Low quality with labels and hitboxes intact.
  • Gameplay remains authoritative and unchanged: item generation, stats, economy, drop odds, ownership, lifetime, interaction radius, pickup confirmation, inventory behavior, and save data are untouched.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-30.

Patch 0.41.0.29 (every menu sigil is codeborn)

  • Every ability now bears its own generated sigil: all 52 selectable class abilities plus the Frost Nova compatibility route receive a crisp dark-fantasy icon derived from the same class palette, relic family, and semantic identity as the spell itself.
  • The whole armory speaks one visual language: all 36 equipment families now use code-generated inventory art keyed to their real wearable descriptor, so weapons, armor, jewelry, offhands, and every slot remain visually connected to what appears on the character.
  • Item history remains visible at a glance: rarity, level, potency, sockets, socketed-gem colors, set allegiance, and unique effects add restrained marks without obscuring each item's core silhouette.
  • Soulstones have become a complete family: all seven gem types across all six qualities have distinct generated color, facet, and quality marks, while Eidolon Hearts and Shards receive their own enduring-soul and broken-prism relics.
  • Every item-facing window uses the same source of truth: inventory, character equipment, vendor, stash, buyback, forge, and trading routes now ask the procedural registry for art instead of trusting old persisted file paths.
  • Old saves stay safe: legacy icon strings may remain in historical player records, but clients deliberately ignore them; item identity, equipment, progression, stats, economy, and save compatibility are unchanged.
  • The old painted icon vault is gone: 137 superseded ability, equipment, and gem files plus both multi-megabyte currency bitmaps have left the production tree, removing roughly 165 MB without touching terrain or environmental imagery.
  • Missing art can no longer hide: coverage cross-checks the authoritative server loot catalog against client items and procedural descriptors, validates all 53 ability identities and 80 item/currency/gem identities, and fails closed on unknown content instead of drawing a generic placeholder.
  • The browser gallery now opens the reliquary: dedicated hardware-rendered ability, armory, and soulstone contact sheets verify unique keys, complete image decode, generated metadata, cache reuse, and clear readability at real UI scale.
  • Asset failures are visible again: because generated data icons make no network request, the browser gate no longer suppresses canceled legacy icon fetches; any new authored dependency will fail loudly.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-29.

Patch 0.41.0.28 (every wound answers with a relic)

  • Every combat outcome now leaves an intentional mark: Fighter, Rogue, Wizard, Cleric, hostile, and reflected hits each receive a compact code-generated dark-fantasy reaction instead of relying on floating numbers alone.
  • Afflictions speak their own language: bleed drips through a blood-tithe seal and poison blooms from a venom censer, keeping repeated damage readable without pretending it was another direct strike.
  • Every realm hazard wounds differently: lava, gravewind sandstorm, lightning, and wind damage use distinct cinder, grit, storm-brand, and gale-shear reactions derived from the exact authoritative hazard kind.
  • Recovery is no longer one anonymous green flash: Cleric healing, recurring restoration, lifesteal, and self-restoration now gather through separate mercy, rosary, sanguine, and pale-heart relics.
  • Damage and healing carry server truth: authoritative payloads now include semantic kind and instance identity across direct abilities, projectiles, zones, ailments, reflection, kill effects, and restoration.
  • Dungeon combat stays inside its instance: damage and healing broadcasts are routed by instance, while open-world hazard messages retain their shared overworld behavior.
  • Existing combat cues remain intact: floating numbers and involvement audio still report magnitude and urgency; the new victim-side relics complement cast and projectile art without replacing or duplicating it.
  • Busy fights stay clean: reactions are proximity-filtered and throttled per target and effect kind, so rapid ticks cannot bury actors while simultaneous bleed, poison, and direct damage remain distinguishable.
  • High and Low quality preserve the same identity: both tiers keep the core wound seal and witness halo, while Low removes only optional shards; cached immutable geometry and materials keep concurrent effects independent and cheap.
  • The browser audit now witnesses consequence and recovery: dedicated damage and restoration galleries verify all 16 identities for visible finite geometry, unique motifs, shared-cache safety, and complete cleanup.
  • Combat balance is unchanged: damage, healing, tick timing, cooldowns, resource costs, target rules, and authoritative ability footprints remain exactly where gameplay logic placed them.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-28.

Patch 0.41.0.27 (every projectile lands with consequence)

  • Every collision-capable projectile and trap now leaves its own mark: Fireball, Arcane Missile, Dragonfire Lance, Dagger, Flame Tornado, Meteor, Phantom Arrow, Tripwire, Explosive Trap, and Snare Trap each resolve through an intentional code-generated dark-fantasy impact instead of a shared flash.
  • Impact timing now belongs to the server: multiplayer clients present collisions only from a new authoritative impact event, removing the duplicate bursts, early removals, and visual disagreement caused by client-side collision guesses.
  • Area impacts show their real reach: Fireball draws its ten-unit blast, Explosive Trap draws its six-unit detonation, and every Meteor rune draws the exact landing radius supplied by authoritative combat logic.
  • Boundaries stay honest while the magic moves: each area fill and outer edge remains fixed at gameplay size while crowns, seals, hearts, shards, and binding lines animate inside it; Low quality keeps the same combat footprint.
  • Piercing and bouncing attacks acknowledge every real victim: Dagger, Dragonfire Lance, and Flame Tornado can present each server-confirmed target impact without collapsing later contacts into the first hit.
  • Expired projectiles no longer pretend they struck something: ordinary lifetime cleanup is silent, while Meteor retains a deduplicated packet-loss fallback so a real landing cannot disappear or play twice.
  • Offline combat closes its old collision holes: Phantom Arrow and all three Rogue trap families now use the same typed impact route, and local Fireball, Explosive Trap, and Meteor splash checks use their authoritative footprints.
  • Dungeon and overworld traffic stays in its lane: impact events are filtered by instance and distant overworld events are ignored unless their source or projectile is relevant to the local client.
  • Impact art is fast and independently disposable: immutable geometry and materials are cached, every effect owns its transform and teardown, and removing one impact cannot invalidate another still on screen.
  • The browser audit watches every collision family: dedicated direct-hit and area galleries verify all ten types for unique identity, visible finite geometry, and exact AOE boundaries, while unit and server coverage prove High/Low construction, cleanup, payload truth, and duplicate suppression.
  • Combat balance is unchanged: damage, cooldowns, resource costs, target rules, and server-owned radii remain intact; stale offline splash checks and visuals were aligned to those existing authoritative values.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-27.

Patch 0.41.0.26 (every ability cast becomes a rite)

  • All 52 selectable abilities now cast with an intentional identity: every Fighter, Rogue, Wizard, and Cleric presentation leaves the generic transient-effect palette for a named code-generated dark-fantasy rite.
  • Class fantasy carries through the full cast: Fighter abilities use siege wakes, war-oaths, bulwarks, and headsman wheels; Rogue abilities use blackglass blades, execution seals, venom sacraments, and eclipse shrouds.
  • Wizard and Cleric magic no longer share anonymous shapes: extinction clocks, furnace lenses, void astrolabes, mercy fonts, oath chapels, rescue wings, and last-bell decrees give each spell a distinct silhouette and palette.
  • Shield Slam finally shows its whole hit area: the cast now draws the authoritative four-unit, ninety-degree cone in addition to its target impact instead of pretending a point flash is the entire attack.
  • Every authoritative area remains exact: circular and conical gameplay boundaries carry the same radius and arc used by combat logic, stay fixed while interior relics animate, and retain that truth on Low graphics.
  • Frost Nova keeps its own winter language: the compatibility ability resolves through Flame Whip's canonical gameplay route while presenting an eight-unit rimeglass nova and winter-chain seal rather than fire.
  • Replicated casts preserve semantic identity: every remote layer now enters the same production dispatcher with canonical ability, requested alias, direction, layer index, radius, and arc instead of dropping back to anonymous point effects.
  • Generic actor wrappers no longer erase class art: remote visual resolution prefers the entity's declared mesh/class type, and the modern dispatcher no longer depends on an obsolete per-entity fallback method.
  • Cast resources are shared without shared state: immutable geometry and materials are cached by ability while each local or remote cast owns its transforms and teardown cannot invalidate a surviving peer.
  • The browser audit now checks what the player actually sees: all 112 base/rune presentations are verified in High and Low hardware Chrome for layer count, canonical/requested identity, unique motif, visible geometry, finite transforms, and exact boundaries.
  • Combat balance is unchanged: damage, cooldowns, mana, targeting, server authority, and existing radius values remain on their established paths; this patch makes their presentation truthful and distinctive.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-26.
